framework.name: ACTFL World-Readiness Standards for Learning Languages
framework.source: https://www.actfl.org/educator-resources/world-readiness-standards-for-learning-languages (codes are the standard numbers; objective wording is the school's own)

objectives.description: Greet people, introduce yourself and say goodbye in Spanish, using formal and informal forms.
Ask and answer questions about names, age and where you are from.
Recognize the sounds of the Spanish alphabet and read simple words aloud with correct pronunciation.
Understand numbers from 0 to 100 and use them for ages, prices and phone numbers.
Exchange information about days, dates and the weather.
Present information about yourself and your family in a short spoken or written description.
Identify the main idea of a short text about a family or a school.
Describe people using ser and common adjectives that agree in gender and number.
Talk about classes, school supplies and what you need, using tener and hay.
Say what you like and do not like with gustar, and ask a classmate the same.
Write a short paragraph about your schedule and your favorite subjects.
Tell time and say when classes begin and end.
Use regular -ar verbs in the present tense to say what people do.
Compare greetings and personal space in Spanish-speaking countries with those in your community.
Describe a product or tradition from a Spanish-speaking country, such as Day of the Dead or la quinceañera.
Use Spanish to learn about geography by naming the countries and capitals of Spanish-speaking nations.
Notice similarities between Spanish and English words, including cognates and false friends.
Find examples of Spanish in your community, such as signs, menus and media, and report what they say.
Review greetings and introductions, and talk about family, school and free time in complete sentences.
Describe your daily routine using reflexive verbs such as despertarse and ducharse.
Understand a short recording or text about a typical day.
Use stem-changing verbs in the present tense to express wants, preferences and abilities.
Talk about household chores and your home using vocabulary for rooms and furniture.
Write a description of your home and neighborhood.
Use ir a plus an infinitive to talk about plans for the weekend.
Order food in a restaurant and discuss meals and food preferences.
Read a menu and recipe and understand the quantities and steps.
Use direct object pronouns to avoid repetition when talking about food and shopping.
Present a short talk about a traditional dish and where it comes from.
Talk about clothes and shopping, including prices, sizes and colors.
Make comparisons with más que, menos que and tan como.
Compare mealtimes and eating customs in Spain, Mexico and the United States.
Describe the foods and markets of a Spanish-speaking region.
Use Spanish to learn about nutrition or geography from a Spanish-language source.
Explain a difference in school or home life between a Spanish-speaking country and your own.
Set a goal for using Spanish outside the classroom and track it for a week.
Talk about your past experiences and what you did last weekend using the preterite.
Write a paragraph about a trip you took, with times and places.
Understand the main ideas and details of a travel story in Spanish.
Contrast the preterite and the imperfect to describe what used to happen and what happened once.
Narrate a childhood memory with background details and key events.
Use irregular preterite verbs correctly in conversation.
Make and respond to requests for help and directions in a city.
Read an authentic ad or a brochure and identify its purpose.
Talk about health, symptoms and visiting a doctor.
Use commands to give advice, instructions and directions.
Give a short presentation that offers advice on a healthy lifestyle.
Use indirect object pronouns with verbs such as dar, decir and gustar.
Explain how holidays and family celebrations differ in Spanish-speaking countries.
Describe a piece of art, music or literature from the Spanish-speaking world.
Use Spanish to learn about history or science from an authentic source.
Compare a Spanish-language news report with an English one on the same topic.
Explain how Spanish expresses the past differently from English.
Interview a Spanish speaker in your community, with preparation, and report what you learned.
Discuss current events and personal opinions in Spanish using a range of tenses.
Understand the main points and supporting details of an authentic news article.
Express wishes, doubts and emotions with the present subjunctive.
Make recommendations and persuade others using the subjunctive after verbs of influence.
Write a formal email to a company or school in Spanish.
Read a short story in Spanish and identify the characters, setting and conflict.
Hold a discussion about a theme from the story, giving reasons and examples.
Talk about the future using the future tense and the conditional.
Present your plans for college and work after high school in Spanish.
Listen to a podcast or a news broadcast and summarize it.
Use relative clauses and connectors to give longer and more detailed answers.
Write a persuasive essay about an issue that matters in your community.
Analyze how a social issue, such as immigration, is viewed in different Spanish-speaking communities.
Analyze a work of art or a film from the Spanish-speaking world for its message.
Use Spanish to gather information on a topic from another subject area.
Compare how a cultural practice or perspective differs between your community and one in a Spanish-speaking country.
Use Spanish in a community setting, such as volunteering or interpreting, and reflect on it.
Create a portfolio of your Spanish for a college or career audience.
Greet people, introduce yourself and say goodbye in French, using tu and vous.
Ask and answer questions about names, age and where you are from.
Recognize French sounds, accents and liaison, and read simple words aloud.
Understand numbers from 0 to 100 and use them for ages, prices and phone numbers.
Exchange information about days, dates and the weather.
Present information about yourself and your family in a short spoken or written description.
Describe people using être and adjectives that agree in gender and number.
Talk about school, classes and supplies using avoir and il y a.
Say what you like and do not like with aimer and préférer.
Tell time and say when classes begin and end.
Use regular -er verbs in the present tense to say what people do.
Write a short paragraph about your schedule and your favorite subjects.
Find the main idea in a short text about a French school.
Compare greetings, such as la bise and the handshake, in France and the French-speaking world.
Describe a product or tradition from a French-speaking country.
Name the French-speaking countries and their capitals on a map.
Notice similarities between French and English words, including cognates.
Find examples of French in your community, such as products and signs, and report what they say.
Review greetings and introductions, and talk about family, school and free time in complete sentences.
Describe your daily routine using reflexive verbs such as se réveiller and se laver.
Understand a short recording or text about a typical day.
Use aller plus an infinitive to talk about plans.
Order food in a café or restaurant and discuss meals and food preferences.
Read a menu and recipe and understand the quantities and steps.
Use partitive articles to talk about food and drink.
Present a short talk about a traditional dish and where it comes from.
Talk about clothes and shopping, including prices, sizes and colors.
Use the passé composé with avoir to talk about what happened yesterday.
Use the passé composé with être for verbs of movement.
Write a paragraph about your last weekend.
Make comparisons with plus que, moins que and aussi que.
Compare mealtimes and eating customs in France, Senegal and the United States.
Describe the food and markets of a French-speaking region.
Use French to learn about nutrition or geography from a French-language source.
Explain a difference in school or home life between a French-speaking country and your own.
Set a goal for using French outside the classroom and track it for a week.
